title: [WT-06] Wrappers: Serena root, shared memory and skills links, and the link manifest
description:
Plan against docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §5.2 (skills link), §5.3, §5.4 and §1.10 (write side).

Objective: a seat in W gets LSP over the task's own bytes while sharing the project's Serena memories and Claude skills with every other seat, and every link it makes is recorded so removal (WT-14) can unlink it safely.

Deliverable, in scripts/moe-agent.sh and scripts/moe-agent.ps1 as twins:
- Serena root: when the resolved Serena root is the control checkout (the default), it becomes W. A serenaProject or MOE_SERENA_PROJECT override that resolves outside the control checkout is kept and prints MOE_WORKTREE_SERENA_OUTSIDE.
- Links:
  - W/.serena/memories → <control>/.serena/memories
  - W/.claude/skills → <control>/.claude/skills
  - Each is a symlink on Linux and a directory junction on Windows, and is appended to <gitdir>/moe/worktree/<taskId>.links (one W-relative path per line).
  - A failed link prints MOE_WORKTREE_LINK_FAILED; the seat launches without that tool, never with a control-rooted fallback.
- Copy <control>/.serena/project.yml into W with its project_name line rewritten to <name>@<taskId>; nothing is copied when it is missing.
- For each tracked package-lock.json directory in W without node_modules, print MOE_WORKTREE_DEPS_MISSING <dir>, and add one worktree-mode prompt line telling the worker to run `npm ci --prefer-offline` (plus `npm run build` where tests need dist/) before testing that package. Nothing is linked for node_modules.
- Cases in scripts/tests/postflight.sh and postflight.ps1. Depends on WT-05 (task-c4cccb84948c472d93263c9de60fed1d).

NOT in scope: removal or unlinking (WT-14); landing (WT-07 onward); installing dependencies; docs (WT-18).

Verification: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh (and on a Windows seat: node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell)
definitionOfDone: postflight case (both harnesses): the Serena server written for the seat is rooted at W by default; an override outside the control checkout is kept and prints MOE_WORKTREE_SERENA_OUTSIDE.
postflight case: W/.serena/memories and W/.claude/skills resolve to the control checkout's directories, and both paths are listed in <gitdir>/moe/worktree/<taskId>.links.
postflight case: W/.serena/project.yml exists with project_name '<name>@<taskId>'; a forced link failure prints MOE_WORKTREE_LINK_FAILED and the seat still launches.
postflight case: a tracked package-lock.json directory without node_modules prints MOE_WORKTREE_DEPS_MISSING <dir>, and no node_modules link is created anywhere in W.
Both wrappers carry the same MOE_WORKTREE_/MOE_LAND_/MOE_CONTROL_/MOE_BOARD_ codes (grep -oE diff over moe-agent.sh vs moe-agent.ps1 is empty).
The verification command exits 0; postflight.ps1 passes via node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell.

implementationPlan.description: 1. Resolve the seat's Serena root before WT-05 writes configs (tests first). Goal: task-local LSP plus shared tooling without changing shared mode. Architecture: extend the claim-pinned WT-04/WT-05 pre-launch tooling phase, not the early shared-mode writer; keep MOE_PROJECT_PATH and proxy executable rooted at control. Tech: Bash/Python/Node stdlib and Windows PowerShell 5.1-compatible primitives. Read the landed WT-05 phase and docs/plans/2026-10-30-per-task-worktrees.md §5.2-5.4 and §1.10; WT-05 helper names were not yet present at planning, so use its landed entry point rather than inventing a second launch path. Existing verified seams: sh ensure_mcp_config, SERENA_PROJECT/SERENA_CMD and MEMORIES_DIR; ps1 $serenaProject/$serenaPath, $mcpConfigObj and $memoriesDir. Preserve config-over-env-over-default precedence from control/.moe-agent.json. Resolve/normalize paths before comparison; equal-to-control (including explicit equivalent spelling) maps to W; a distinct explicit root is retained, with MOE_WORKTREE_SERENA_OUTSIDE when outside control. A root inside control but not equal remains an explicit override, not silently rewritten. Invalid override keeps existing warning/fallback semantics, but the fallback then maps to W. Pseudocode: `effective = samePath(resolved, control) ? W : resolved; if (explicit && outsideControl(effective) && !samePath(effective,W)) warn(...)`. Use ordinal comparison after the existing platform normalization; use path-component boundaries, not string-prefix containment, and literal paths in PS. Reset effective values per iteration. Add parameterized cases to both harnesses using WT-05 fake launches: all four CLI configs contain the expected --project; explicit control equivalence; env outside root; config beats env; missing override; shared mode unchanged; two launches do not retain the prior W/disabled state. Assert the Moe server still names control and control config bytes are unchanged. This task edits only the four named files; no landing, installation, runtime .moe writes, docs sweep, or prerequisite reimplementation.

2. Provision the two shared links and their manifest with non-destructive error handling. Add one small twin helper called in the worktree tooling phase before configs and memory preload. Fixed pairs only: `.serena/memories` -> control/.serena/memories and `.claude/skills` -> control/.claude/skills. Use the control checkout's resolved common Git directory for `moe/worktree/<taskId>.links`, never W/.git (a file) or .moe. Create only W-local parents; reject parents that resolve outside W. Use native symlinks on Linux/macOS/WSL and directory junctions on native Windows, including Git Bash with native Node: the existing Node executable can use `fs.symlinkSync(target, dest, process.platform === 'win32' ? 'junction' : 'dir')`; PS can use `New-Item -ItemType Junction`. Pass paths as arguments, not interpolated shell commands; preserve spaces/Unicode. Source must be a directory; a missing source, existing real destination, wrong/dangling link, reparse-parent collision or IO failure warns MOE_WORKTREE_LINK_FAILED with the relative path and continues without enabling that shared tool; never delete/replace existing bytes or redirect Serena to control. A matching existing link is reused. Persist each allowed W-relative path once, forward slashes and LF, UTF-8 without BOM; retain earlier entries. Before creating a link, persist its manifest reservation (after validating the destination) so a crash can never leave an unrecorded link; an unused reservation after failed creation is harmless and must not be treated as a removable real directory. Manifest-write failure prevents creating/enabling that link. A memories failure clears the launch-local Serena executable/entry, including stale JSON/TOML entries for every CLI, and suppresses memory preload; a skills failure does not disable Moe or a healthy Serena. Do not alter global/control configs. Tests first in both harnesses: exact realpath target and native link type, manifest set equals the two paths, rerun does not duplicate, control sentinel unchanged, missing source, occupied destination, wrong link, forced creation failure and manifest-write failure. Assert fake CLI still launches with Moe and no Serena after a memories failure, while an independent skills failure leaves Serena enabled. Test helpers must unlink their own junctions/symlinks before scratch-directory cleanup; production removal remains WT-14.

3. Copy and task-qualify Serena project metadata, without modifying control. During the same worktree preparation, copy control/.serena/project.yml into W/.serena/project.yml when the source exists, replacing only the top-level project_name scalar with `<name>@<taskId>` and preserving other settings. Read from control on each preparation, never suffix the prior W copy twice. Preserve scalar escaping for ordinary single-quoted, double-quoted and plain names, comments and CRLF/LF; append the suffix inside existing quotes, or emit a quoted scalar for a plain value. If the name is absent/empty, use control's directory name before the suffix and write one top-level project_name. Missing source means no copy (do not invent a project.yml or remove an existing W file). Reject a destination/parent link that would write outside W; an unreadable source, unsupported non-scalar name, or copy/write failure follows WT-05's config-error route: MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED, report_blocked, no CLI and no partial replacement. Use a temp sibling plus atomic replacement, with cleanup on failure. Add compact table-driven cases in each harness for quoted/plain name and line endings, two tasks get distinct names, repeat stays single-suffixed, all non-name settings preserved and control bytes unchanged, missing source, and failed copy/no launch. Example assertion: `assert.equal(projectName(W), 'fixture@task-postflight')`; name parsing in the fixture must inspect the value rather than merely grep for the task id.

4. Report per-worktree dependency readiness without installing or linking anything. Before launch in worktree mode only, enumerate tracked lockfiles from W using `git -C W ls-files -z --cached -- package-lock.json ':(glob)**/package-lock.json'`, parse NUL records, deduplicate directories and check the basename exactly. Root package prints `.`; nested packages print W-relative forward-slash directories. Do not recursively scan the filesystem, follow a dependency link, or count untracked lockfiles. For each directory lacking a real node_modules directory emit `MOE_WORKTREE_DEPS_MISSING <dir>`; the wrapper never creates/links node_modules or runs npm/build. Add exactly one prompt line per worktree launch: `Before testing a package in this worktree, run npm ci --prefer-offline in that package, plus npm run build where its tests require dist/.` Put it in the common WT-05 prompt/context construction so claude/codex/gemini/grok all receive it, including interactive launches. A git enumeration failure reports MOE_WORKTREE_CREATE_FAILED and uses WT-05's no-launch/report_blocked route rather than pretending the check succeeded. Test in both harnesses: root and space-containing nested tracked packages missing dependencies, an installed package, an untracked lockfile and a control-only node_modules sentinel; assert the exact warning set, exactly one prompt line, zero newly created node_modules links/directories, unchanged control dependency bytes and no npm invocation. Retain the existing shared-mode fixture expectations, with no new dependency prompt or warnings there.

5. Run the single focused verification gate and retain fresh evidence. Add a small assertion in the twin postflight cases comparing sorted unique `/MOE_(?:WORKTREE|LAND|CONTROL|BOARD)_[A-Z0-9_]+/g` token sets from both wrappers; do not edit parity-check.sh (its permanent family expansion belongs to WT-19). Run from repository root exactly `node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs bash && bash scripts/tests/parity-check.sh`. On the required native Windows seat also run `node scripts/tests/postflight-safe.mjs powershell` against the same revision; pwsh alone is not a substitute for Windows PowerShell 5.1. Require exit 0, safe-harness failureClass NONE and parity PASS, no skipped platform evidence represented as passing. Use the safe runner, not raw harness output; harness fixtures can contain adversarial prompt text. Capture command, exitCode and outputTail for complete_task and record Windows evidence. Keep this mid-epic gate scoped to launcher harnesses: no daemon/IDE full regression, dependency installation work or docs sweep. If a final review requires edits, rerun this same gate on the final bytes.

6. Final adversarial self-review, then hand off to QA. Load adversarial-self-review and inspect only this task's diff once: can repeated/concurrent task launches overwrite the manifest or double-suffix a name; can a failed append leave an unrecorded junction; can a stale Serena config route edits to control; can missing/hostile paths, Unicode, trailing separators, symlinked parents or PowerShell wildcard expansion write outside W; does an optional link failure preserve bytes and launch with Moe; do tests clean junctions without deleting shared targets; are node_modules and .moe untouched? Check all six DoD items against concrete twin test assertions, including Windows evidence and code-family equality. Preserve peer dirt and keep the task-wide non-board diff within the 400-net-line cap by reusing WT-05 fixtures and existing writers rather than duplicating launch branches. Fix defects within these four files and repeat the named gate if bytes changed. No Git staging/commit commands: wrappers own delivery. Complete through moe.complete_task with fresh verification evidence; record any non-obvious implementation findings for QA. Full-epic docs and adversarial coverage remain WT-18/WT-19.

comments.content:
@architect-eb7de546 WT-04's planner here. WT-04 (task-c20464ff, rev 1) gives you these:
- W: sh MOE_WT_PATH, MOE_WT_BRANCH, MOE_WT_TARGET and MOE_WT_MODE. ps1 $script:MoeWtPath and its siblings. They are set only after a successful provision.
- Refusal helper: worktree_stop CODE DETAIL / Stop-MoeWorktreeSeat. It calls report_blocked once, then exits 1. Use it for any fatal error. MOE_WORKTREE_LINK_FAILED is a warning per §5, so don't route that one through it.
- Shared suite: scripts/tests/postflight-worktree.cjs (WT-04T, task-dd5daa4b). Add your link and Serena cases there.
- Codes diff (DoD): WT-04 renames the sh-only MOE_LAND_* env-bridge names to MOE_PY_*, so the diff starts empty.
- Comments count: the grep reads comments, so every MOE_WORKTREE_* token you add must appear in both wrappers.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: Reuse WT-05's claim-pinned tooling/config phase and existing serializers; native filesystem links, no new dependencies or helper files. Rejected control-root fallback, copying shared memories, linking node_modules, global config rewrites and implementing WT-14 removal here.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: Verified sh ensure_mcp_config currently computes and exports SERENA_PROJECT once and feeds JSON/TOML writers; ps1 computes $serenaProject/$serenaPath and reuses them in four writers. Memory preload reads those roots. WT-05 is a declared prerequisite under active planning, not yet landed; consume its eventual seam before config writes and preload. Existing Test-MoeSymlink deliberately excludes junctions, so it is not a junction detector. parity-check.sh does not yet compare worktree code families.
planningNotes.risks: Link manifests protect shared targets from future removal, so reserve entries before creation and never recurse through links in test cleanup. Native Windows/Git Bash junction behavior and PS5.1 Unicode/ordinal path identity require actual Windows evidence. Four-file twin change is sized as one ≤60-minute slice by reusing predecessor fixtures; do not extend landing or cleanup scope.
